notes: From the above, it is seen that most of the undertrial prisoners were released from detention in
less than one year in most of the States. The percentage of released undertrials varied from 41.9 in
Jammu & Kashmir to 100 at Dadra & Nagar Haveli. The percentage of undertrial inmates who were
released after a detention whose period is upto 1 year in other states is as follows: Tripura (99.8%),
Kerala (99.5%), Himachal Pradesh (99.2%), Tamil Nadu (97.4%), Chandigarh (96.9%), Meghalaya
(96.8%), Uttar Pradesh (95.9%), Mizoram (94%), Goa (92.6%), Karnataka (90.4%), Assam (89.3%),
Manipur (88.6%), Andaman & Nicobar Island (85.2%), Orissa (84.9%), Rajasthan (84.7%), Sikkim
(84.7%), Bihar (80.4%), Maharashtra (79.3%) and UT of Delhi (76.5%).
From the above table, it is evident that except Bihar, Kerala, Maharashtra, Orissa, Rajasthan and
Delhi in most of the States/UTs very large number of women undertrials were released well below
completion of 1 year of detention during 1995. Such release was 100% in Goa, Himachal Pradesh,
Karnataka, Sikkim, Tripura, Andaman & Nicobar Island and Dadra & Nagar Haveli. Bihar (97), Delhi
(35), Kerala (32), Maharashtra (26), Orissa (17) and Rajasthan (11) reported considerable women
undertrials who remained in custody for 1-2 years in 1995.
Cases uf wamen undertrial prisoners being kept for 2-3 years were reported from 10 states and
one UT during 1995. These States were Assam (1), Bihar (31), Jammu & Kashmir (1), Kerala (8),
Maharashtra (30), Manipur (2), Orissa (3), Rajasthan (5), Tamil Nadu (2), Uttar Pradesh (1) & UT of
Delhi (32). The women undertrial prisoners who stayed in the jails well beyond 3 years but upto 5
years were in 4 states and one UT only viz. Bihar (15), Jammu & Kashmir (3), Kerala (1), Maharashtra
(5) and UT of Delhi (4).
In Maharashtra, 3 women undertrials had been kept for over 5 years without their case coming
to a logical end. Likewise, a solitary case of such a long detention of women prisoner one each also
reported from Orissa State and UT of Delhi.
As seen above, a large number of prison inmates are undergoing/engaged in various vocational
programmes. Bihar, which was mainly engaged in adult education of the prisoners and otherwise
training programmes was reported to have involved the highest number of jail inmates (4913) in its
programmes. This was followed by Uttar Pradesh (1296), Karnataka (942) and Delhi (844).
Productivity by Jail inmates
The training in vocational trades and the regular pursuit by the jail inmates accounted for certain
produce which had market value, resulting into gainful productivity by the prison inmates during 1995.
